_handoff.scopeNote: Official-source pass for obtaining or registering a death certificate for an event in Bengaluru. Only public BBMP/GBA, Government of Karnataka e-JanMa/Chief Registrar material, India Code, and Government Services Portal material was inspected. No login, deceased-person data, application, payment, upload, or certificate lookup was performed. Current portal routing and case-specific registrar remain potentially jurisdiction-dependent.

meta.title: Bengaluru death certificate official-source pass
meta.disclaimer: Research handoff, not official advice. Confirm the event location, registration status, registrar, and current portal route before submitting any death-registration or certificate request.

sources.title: Greater Bengaluru Authority official home
sources.publisher: Greater Bengaluru Authority / Government of Karnataka
sources.notes: Current public home page lists Birth & Death Certificate as an e-service and publishes helpline 1533. The page does not expose a case form in the unauthenticated text view.

sources.title: BBMP citizen services directory
sources.notes: Official directory lists Online Birth Certificate Request Form and Authenticity of Certificates under Birth & Death Certificate. It does not show the current case-specific death form fields in the public directory text.

sources.title: Births and Deaths — Office of the Chief Registrar of Births and Deaths, Karnataka
sources.publisher: Government of Karnataka / Directorate of Economics and Statistics
sources.notes: Government-hosted official page snapshot identifies e-JanMa, urban/BBMP registration by Health Officers/Health Inspectors, private-hospital reporting, certificate download, verification, application-status, additional-copy/correction contacts, and the e-JanMa URL.

sources.title: Training Manual for Civil Registration — Birth and Death
sources.notes: 2012 manual. It describes Form 6 for deaths, the first extract/certificate under section 12, and registration reporting within 21 days; its age means current digital route and fees must be confirmed.

sources.title: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969
sources.notes: India Code public Act record. Sections 8, 10, 12, and 13 provide the statutory framework for persons responsible to report, medical cause information, certificate of registration, and delayed registration; verify current amendments/rules.

sources.title: Karnataka Administrative Reforms — BBMP Birth/Death service audit
sources.notes: 2023 administrative-reforms report says designated officers include Medical Officer/Deputy MO/Superintendent in large hospitals/Assistant Statistical Officer and records a Sakala target of 3 days where online data is available and 7 days where it is not. It also records process-audit observations; this is not treated as a universal current guarantee.

claims.text: The current Greater Bengaluru Authority public home lists Birth & Death Certificate as an e-service and publishes helpline 1533.
claims.notes: The public page does not disclose a death-specific form or case result.

claims.text: The BBMP citizen-services directory lists an Online Birth Certificate Request Form and an Authenticity Of Certificates route under Birth & Death Certificate.
claims.notes: The legacy directory does not prove the current death-certificate form URL, required fields, or that every death use case is online.

claims.text: Karnataka's official Chief Registrar/e-JanMa material states that deaths in urban local-body and BBMP areas are registered in e-JanMa by Health Officers and Health Inspectors, while deaths in private hospitals are reported by the concerned private hospital to the respective Registrar.
claims.notes: Official page snapshot is public guidance; exact current registrar assignment is event/locality-specific.

claims.text: The official Karnataka e-JanMa material publishes public tools for certificate download, birth/death verification, application status, and registration details, and directs additional copies or corrections to the concerned Nadakacheri/data-entry operator and registration centre.
claims.notes: The public material does not establish which input fields or records a particular Bengaluru event will require.

claims.text: The BBMP civil-registration manual identifies Form 6 as the death-report form and says information reported within 21 days is eligible for a free first extract under section 12; the manual is from 2012 and current fees/route are not inferred.
claims.notes: Historic official manual; current law/rules and portal implementation may differ.

claims.text: A BBMP/Karnataka administrative-reforms report records a Sakala time limit of 3 days where online data is available and 7 days where it is not for issue of birth, still-birth, and death certificates.
claims.notes: Report wording is not treated as a current unconditional SLA; it also records process-audit observations.

claims.text: The Registration of Births and Deaths Act provides the statutory framework for reporting deaths, issuing a registration extract/certificate, and delayed registration, but the Act alone does not identify the current Bengaluru portal route or case-specific document checklist.
claims.notes: Check current amendments and Karnataka rules before giving legal/procedural advice.

roadblocks.title: Current death-certificate portal route not fully exposed
roadblocks.symptom: Current GBA/BBMP pages list Birth & Death service links but public text does not show the current death form fields or event-specific route.
roadblocks.likelyCause: Legacy directory, JavaScript service link, and e-JanMa/local registrar channels have different public surfaces.
roadblocks.recovery: Start from the current GBA/BBMP Birth & Death service link or Karnataka e-JanMa public tools and confirm the event's registrar before entering data.

roadblocks.title: Registered versus unregistered event
roadblocks.symptom: Public pages cannot tell whether a death record exists, is digitized, or needs first registration, delayed registration, correction, or a duplicate copy.
roadblocks.likelyCause: Requires event date/place and registrar record lookup.
roadblocks.recovery: Classify the case first; do not use a certificate-download route as a substitute for registration or delayed-registration permission.

roadblocks.title: Legacy manual and report caveats
roadblocks.symptom: The Form 6/21-day manual and Sakala 3/7-day report are older publications than the current GBA/e-JanMa presentation.
roadblocks.likelyCause: Rules, portal ownership, and service implementation update on different cycles.
roadblocks.recovery: Treat timing/fee statements as leads and verify the current registrar, rules, and service page before submission.
